hero.name: Rajesh
hero.who: a sweet shop owner in Bhopal who plans every year as if it will repeat

story.b: Rajesh has run his family's sweet shop in Bhopal's old city for twenty-two years. Every September, he opens the same red ledger and orders the same amount of khoya, sugar and ghee for Diwali as last year, plus a little extra. It has always worked. He tells his son Kunal that the business is as predictable as the seasons. This year, three weeks before Diwali, the city digs up the road in front of the shop for a new drain. For a month, customers cannot reach his counter. Boxes of kaju katli sit unsold. Rajesh stares at his ledger, which never once mentioned a road being dug up. The past, it turns out, made no promises about the future.

ask.q: Rajesh is shocked that his reliable ledger failed him. What is the most useful lesson?
o: Last year's pattern is no guarantee, so prepare for surprises he cannot predict
This was bad luck that will never happen again, so change nothing
Study the ledger harder to predict next year exactly
ask.why: Calling it a one-time fluke ignores how often surprises happen, and a more detailed ledger still cannot see what has never happened before. Accepting that the past does not guarantee the future pushes him to build in buffers and flexibility instead.

chapters.take: Yesterday is not a promise about tomorrow.

story.b: While the road is still dug up, a stranger squeezes past the barricades into the shop. She is planning her daughter's wedding and wants three thousand boxes of sweets. Rajesh almost says no, since he has never handled an order that big. He takes it, hires extra karigars and works through the nights. The wedding guests love the sweets. Over the next few months, eleven more families call, each mentioning that wedding. Looking back, Rajesh realises that this one unplanned visit earned more than his whole Diwali season usually does. His steady counter sales kept the lights on. But the year itself was shaped by one event that nobody, including him, saw coming.

ask.q: Kunal asks how to plan for big surprise orders like that wedding. What is the wisest answer?
o: Plan as if a big order will come every month
Ignore it as a fluke and plan only from the daily average
Accept that rare big events shape the year, and stay ready to say yes to them
ask.why: Expecting a big order every month is fantasy, and ignoring it misses the very event that shaped the year. Rare surprises cannot be scheduled, but they are powerful when they come. Keeping some spare capacity and being ready to act lets him catch the good ones.

chapters.take: A few unexpected events can matter more than years of routine.

story.b: Kunal tries to plan next year's staff by averaging the monthly catering orders. Rajesh frowns at the numbers. Counter sales are steady: no single customer buying a kilo of jalebi can change the month much, so averages work there. Catering is a different world. One month might bring nothing, and the next might bring one order bigger than the rest of the year combined. The average describes a month that never actually happens. Rajesh explains this to Kunal over evening chai. For the counter, they can plan calmly. For catering, they need a list of karigars who can be called in at short notice, rather than a fixed number on the payroll.

ask.q: Kunal wants to use average monthly catering orders to decide staff numbers. What is the problem?
o: There is no problem, since averages always describe a business well
In catering one huge order can swamp the rest, so averages mislead
He should simply use last month's number instead of the average
ask.why: Averages work when no single case can move the total much, like daily counter sales. Catering lives in a different zone, where one huge order can outweigh everything else. Using the average, or just last month, hides that reality and leaves them unprepared.

chapters.take: Averages work in calm zones but mislead where one case can dominate.

story.b: Across the street, an old namkeen shop suddenly shuts down. By evening, the chai stall has a dozen confident explanations. The owner's son was lazy. The rent was too high. The quality had dropped. Everyone agrees, as if it was always going to happen. Rajesh finds himself nodding along, then stops. A month ago, the same people said that shop would last forever. He knows the owner's mother fell ill, the drain work blocked their entrance too, and a key supplier quit the same week. Much of it was bad timing and chance. The neat story sounds wise, but it makes everyone feel safer than they really are. Rajesh walks back to his own shop, a little more careful.

ask.q: Kunal says the neighbour closed only because of his lazy son, so they are safe. What should Rajesh tell him?
o: Agree, since the explanation everyone shares must be true
Find an even more detailed explanation that covers every cause
Be wary of neat stories, since much of it was chance and they face risks too
ask.why: A story everyone repeats can still be wrong, and a more detailed one is still a story squeezed out of messy events. Remembering how much was luck and timing keeps them humble and prepared, instead of falsely confident about their own shop.

chapters.take: Neat explanations after the fact can make us falsely confident.

story.b: A friend urges Rajesh to copy a famous sweet brand from another city that grew through franchise outlets. He shows reels about its owner and the simple formula behind it. Rajesh is tempted. Then he asks a different question: who else tried the same thing? Over two weeks of chai and phone calls, he finds four shop owners in Bhopal who franchised the same way. Three quietly shut down within two years, having lost their savings. Nobody makes reels about them. Their stories stay invisible, because failure rarely gets an audience. The formula looked brilliant only because he was seeing the one survivor. Rajesh decides to look far more carefully before risking anything.

ask.q: Kunal's friend wants to drop out of college because a famous founder did. What should Kunal suggest?
o: Look for the many who tried the same path and quietly struggled
Follow the famous founder's path exactly, since it clearly works
Read more interviews with successful dropouts for inspiration
ask.why: Famous success stories hide the many people who did the same things and failed quietly. Copying the path or reading more winners' interviews only shows the survivors. Looking for those who struggled gives a far more honest picture before such a big decision.

chapters.take: Before copying a winner, look for those who tried and quietly failed.

story.b: Kunal has a bold idea: selling low-sugar sweets online to Bhopal families with older parents. He wants to put all their savings into it. Rajesh does not want to risk everything, but he does not want to shut the door either. They agree on a different plan. The main shop stays steady and careful, with most savings in a fixed deposit and a reserve for surprises like the dug-up road. They put a small amount, money they could lose without real harm, into a three-month online trial. If it fails, they lose a little. If it takes off, it could one day become bigger than the shop. Kunal is thrilled. Rajesh sleeps well too.

ask.q: Rajesh's cousin wants to try a bold new business idea. Which approach fits best?
o: Put all his savings into it, since big bets bring big rewards
Keep most of his money safe and try the idea with a small, affordable amount
Avoid any new idea, since the future is unpredictable
ask.why: Betting everything risks ruin if the surprise is a bad one, while avoiding all bets shuts out the good surprises. Keeping the core safe and putting only a small, affordable amount into a bold idea limits the downside while leaving room for a big upside.

chapters.take: Keep most of life safe, and make small bets with big upside.

story.b: Weeks later, Diwali comes round again. This time Rajesh does not just copy last year's order. He keeps a buffer of stock and cash, and a phone list of karigars who can come at short notice. Two days before the festival, the power fails across the old city for a whole afternoon. Rajesh is ready with a generator he had booked just in case. The online trial is small but growing, with orders arriving from as far as Indore. At the chai stall, someone confidently explains exactly why the power failed. Rajesh just smiles and sips his tea. He no longer expects to predict the year. He just tries to be ready for whatever it brings.

chapters.take: You cannot predict surprises, but you can be ready for them.
